title: Choose the visual world for Win Equipments
question: The roll assigned the Dew-Point Chart world. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Dew-Point Chart
options.lineage: Psychrometric and dew-point charts every HVAC and compressed-air engineer reads
options.thesis: Show the equipment doing its job: air and water moving from a hot 45°C plant to a guaranteed dew point or leaving temperature, plotted.
materials: chart paper with true measuring rulings
options.viewport: Phone: short headline naming dryers, chillers and FRP cooling towers, Request Quote, then a live chart plotting 45°C inlet air falling to +3°C pressure dew point in green with labelled state points. Desktop: headline left, chart and product photo right.
options.risk: If the chart becomes decoration instead of real numbers it turns into the blueprint-grid costume the old site wore.

raised.raise: Design conditions (45°C ambient, 7 bar, inlet temperature) stay locked as a persistent readout on every product page, like a timecode in its corner.
Colour commits at page scale once: the enquiry close is a full flat #008810 field, not green sprinkled everywhere.
Every working-principle diagram labels each stage and steps through it one stage at a time.
On phones a single vertical capacity axis rules the model ladder in the spec explorer.
Every model row is addressable (e.g. #wrd-500) and its quote link carries the model, so the trail back is exact.

options.label: The Datasheet & GA Drawing
options.lineage: Manufacturer datasheets and general-arrangement drawings with title blocks
options.thesis: The site reads like a well-made engineering datasheet: title block, dimensioned views, revision table.
options.viewport: Product family names set as a datasheet title block, a dimensioned product view, model range table below.
options.risk: Familiar: close to the blueprint look most industrial redesigns land on, and easy to tip into costume.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse Board
options.thesis: Model ranges as a ruled departure board: fixed columns, rows that update in place.
options.viewport: A board of models with capacity, power and connection columns; the selected model flips into view.
options.case: Fuses well for spec tables (product clarity holds) but plant engineers don't identify with rail concourses, and a dark board fights bright factory light.
options.risk: Reads as novelty if the board is used for anything but real model data.

options.label: Emergency Signal Card
options.thesis: Colour bars and a locked timecode.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no audience identification, obscures the offer.

options.label: French Pop Sleeve
options.thesis: One flat saturated ground per release.
options.viewport: Flat colour field with a cropped image.
options.case: Fuses poorly: playful register undermines engineering trust.
options.kept: Total commitment of one flat colour field at page scale.

options.label: Paper Automata
options.thesis: Folds and linkages that move in procession.
options.kept: Every mechanism shows and labels its linkage stage by stage.

options.label: Mesophotic Deep Dive
options.thesis: One vertical depth axis rules everything.
options.case: Fuses poorly: dark, decorative, far from the plant floor.
options.kept: A single vertical measurement axis organising content on phones.

options.label: HyperCard Stack
options.thesis: Linked cards with an exact trail back.
options.case: Fuses poorly: retro-computing has nothing to do with industrial buyers.
options.kept: Every item is deep-linkable and the trail back is exact.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What industrial manufacturers ship (Atlas Copco, ELGi, BEKO), executed with full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Photo hero with headline and Request Quote, category grid, trust strip, industries.
